dialogue.user: Thanks for these options! I'm not set on a specific genre, but could you tell me a bit more about the "Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series"? What's it about?
dialogue.agent:
"Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series" is a historical epic set over 5,000 years ago during the dawn of written history. It follows three shepherd boys who, after witnessing the execution of their families by invaders, rescue eight girls and join a widowed princess on a dangerous trek toward the city of Ausgrenor. The story explores the struggle for survival, the choices between loyalty and escape, and the founding of early city-states in the Fertile Crescent.

The series is intended for readers of all ages. It avoids graphic violence or sexuality and gives perspectives from multiple characters, including orphans, couples, and their adversaries. The setting spans southwestern Iran, southern Iraq, and the Persian Gulf delta, expanding through later books. The writing style presents ancient languages as modern English for accessibility.

Would you like to know what readers thought of this book?

result.title: Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series
result.features: 5,203 years ago, cruel eastern invaders annihilate villages in the wintry Sakros Mountains. Survivors flood west into the fertile plain between the rivers, seeking refuge among its walled cities. Three shepherd boys see their families executed and flee to one of their caves, where they find eight starving girls and bodies of others. Unwilling to abandon them, the boys hide them in a remote cave in the high forest, and feed and equip them until they’re fit to travel. Weida, widowed princess of an overrun kingdom, joins them on their trek to Ausgrenor. She seeks Patros, widower-brother of her late husband. Fortified cities fall. Ausgrenor stands alone. Terrified citizens regress into savagery. Their vicious king plots to rob the rich and flee. Neighboring Bedu tribes slip away into the desert. Invaders approach. Patros is torn between ancestral loyalties and survival of his new wards. Fight or flee. Now or never. Thus begins the six-novel Raising Up Pharaoh epic, set among the emerging city-states and nations in the Fertile Crescent at the dawn of written history—as they plant the cultural seeds of today’s world. The series is written for readers of all ages. The tone is intense, yet controlled by zooming back the lens to avoid needless close-ups of violence and sexuality. The tale unfolds through the differing viewpoints of the orphans, the couple, others drawn to them, and their foes. This first book’s setting ranges across the southwestern mountains of what is now called Iran, southern Iraq between the lower Tigris and Euphrates rivers, the marshes of their delta with the Persian Gulf, and is bounded on the west by the Saudi Arabian desert. In later books, the setting expands throughout the Middle East, the Steppes, West and South Asia, and Northwest Africa. Each book has its own maps. The diverse cast speaks a pidgin of proto-Indo-European, proto-Afro-Semitic, and various lost languages such as Harappan. The pidgin is presented in modern U.S. English. The Raising Up Pharaoh novels were edited by Dr. Dennis E. Hensley PhD

Thairyn and the Thieves
products.description: From the Author I am very excited to have this book finally published! It has taken a long time due to my own moving across the state, building a home and getting resettled in another small town. Thairyn is a wonderful, rascally, regular boy. I love his character, maybe because he reminds me of my own childhood.One thing I know is that I've always wanted a dragon of my own. Maybe more than one. That's why I love fantasy. Dragons fire the imagination with all sorts of possibilities. Were they good or evil? Man killers or friends? What colors were they? Where did they live? Did they hoard treasure or just cause havoc? Come share Thairyn's first real adventure on the magical world of Irth! From the Back Cover Heir to the throne of en'Edlia on the magical world of Irth, Crown Patriarch Thairyn insistently claims that he has a magical birth-gift, even though there is no evidence of it. His family fears he is not just a late bloomer, but magicless like his mother and older sister.The rebellious Xens continue their hostilities against the ruling family members who were born off-world or without magic. When Xens kidnap Thairyn, his frolicking game of "catch-me-if-you-can" turns into a deadly race of "find-me-if-you-can." Will Thairyn be able to overcome his own fear and self-doubt? Will his family be exiled? Will Thairyn escape his kidnappers before they claim the ransom and possibly his life?, p>Unknown to anyone, Thairyn steals a secret that will change all their lives- if there is time for it to unfold amid political and family crisis and the vengeful kidnappers' plot. About the Author A retired reading teacher of 25 years, Nan Whybark loves books and kids and dragons. Putting them all together in one place is what she likes best! Ms. Whybark lives in a small town in Washington state, has five grown children and 20 grandchildren. Read more
